content.text: No audit or inspection right running against PB exists anywhere in the agreement — I'll confirm my reading and submit.

input.quote: 9.1 Accounting. Each Party will maintain materially complete and accurate accounting records related to this Agreement in accordance with GAAP. Each Party will retain such records for [***] after the earlier of expiration or early termination of this Agreement.
input.rationale: The Agreement grants SFJ no audit, inspection or verification right against PB. Article 9 (Records) imposes only mutual record-keeping and retention obligations (Sections 9.1 and 9.2) with no accompanying right of access, examination or on-site review. Section 3.6 ("Audits") does not create any SFJ audit right over PB either: each Party audits its own Permitted Third Parties (3.6.1) and PB audits its own manufacturing facilities (3.6.2), in each case simply sharing the resulting audit reports; similarly, Section 3.5.5 only requires exchange of source data verification reports. The affirmative covenants in Section 7.6, unusually for a secured financing, contain no lender-style inspection/books-and-records access right, and the financial information flow in Section 3.18.2 is limited to delivery of PB's own financial statements plus periodic executive meetings — reporting, not auditing. There is therefore no frequency, notice, cost-allocation or systems-access exposure to constrain, and nothing in the walk-away zone (no unlimited, unannounced or remote-access audit rights). This position is better for us than the playbook's preferred outcome, so no redline is warranted; we would resist any SFJ attempt to add an audit or inspection right, and if one is introduced we would require it to be limited to once per 12 months on 30 days' notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at SFJ's cost absent a >5% discrepancy, with no direct access to PB systems.
